title: Fully differential telescopic OTA
description: A fully differential telescopic-cascode OTA. Each side stacks an input device, an NMOS cascode, a PMOS cascode, and a PMOS load between the rails, above a tail device shared by the two sides; the cascodes boost the output resistance so a single stage reaches high gain. $A_v = g_{m,in} * R_{out}$, where each side's output resistance is a cascode-boosted branch resistance combined in parallel: looking down, the NMOS cascode multiplies the input device's $r_o$ by its intrinsic gain ($A_{v0,cascn}/g_{ds,in}$); looking up, the PMOS cascode multiplies the load's $r_o$ ($A_{v0,cascp}/g_{ds,load}$). Those branch expressions are the standard cascode approximation (they drop second-order $g_{mb}$ and finite-cascode-gain terms). Being fully differential, there is no current-mirror in the signal path and therefore no mirror pole or its attendant pole-zero doublet — a real frequency-response advantage over the single-ended mirror-loaded stage. Common-mode feedback is required to set the output common mode, but the CMFB loop itself is out of this sheet's scope (no loop solving): it appears only as a current line item $I_{cmfb}$ added to the supply budget. The differential output swing is twice the single-ended cascoded headroom. Only the tail's bias reference is programmed, with $I_{tail}$: the tail device shares its gate and width and delivers the programmed current less the mirror's drain-voltage error, and each side carries half of what it delivers, so a design held fixed at another process condition follows its reference instead of carrying a typed current. Internal node levels are authored choice params, and every device in the stack declares that it must stay saturated. On the demo NMOS table every device sizes against the same data.

params.name: v_margin
params.note: headroom beyond the four stacked cascode vdsat drops (tail saturation plus safety) folded into the swing estimate

params.name: I_cmfb
params.note: current the common-mode feedback network draws; the CMFB loop itself is out of scope (no loop solving here) — this is a supply-budget line item only

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node sits below the reference's diode drop); each side carries half of what is delivered, and the supply current is computed from that, not from this number

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion (sets gm_in and input noise)

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: a higher V* costs headroom at the tail node

params.name: V_s
params.note: tail node (input-pair source) DC level. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed (a range end), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

params.name: V_a
params.note: input-device drain / NMOS-cascode source node. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed (a range end), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

params.name: V_out
params.note: output common-mode DC level. A common-mode feedback loop, not drawn on this sheet, holds the outputs here; this is that loop's reference

params.name: V_b
params.note: PMOS-cascode source / load-drain node. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed (a range end), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

params.name: p_sign
params.note: vds sign of the PMOS device tables: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

doc.title: Tail bias reference
doc.description: The diode-connected reference the programmed current $I_{tail}$ flows into — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the tail device needs to copy it.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with the tail node $V_s$ as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at the tail node $V_s$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It has to stay saturated, and it leaves saturation when the tail node $V_s$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which sets the floor under the tail node.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

doc.title: Input pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device, carrying half of what the tail delivers; its gm sets the stage transconductance and its output conductance is the bottom of the down-looking cascode branch.

doc.title: NMOS cascode device
doc.description: The NMOS cascode over the input device; its intrinsic gain multiplies the input device's output resistance (the down-looking branch of Rout).

doc.title: PMOS cascode device
doc.description: The PMOS cascode under the load; its intrinsic gain multiplies the load's output resistance (the up-looking branch of Rout).

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: PMOS load device
doc.description: The PMOS load, in the input device's branch and carrying that device's current; its output conductance is the top of the up-looking cascode branch.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

equations.name: Rdown
equations.note: down-looking branch resistance: the input device ro boosted by the NMOS cascode intrinsic gain (cascode approximation)

equations.name: Rup
equations.note: up-looking branch resistance: the load ro boosted by the PMOS cascode intrinsic gain (cascode approximation)

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: single-side output resistance = the two cascode branches in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: swing_diff
equations.note: differential output swing = twice the single-ended range left after the four stacked cascode vdsat drops and the tail/safety margin

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — what the tail device delivers, plus the CMFB network's budget (the CMFB loop itself is out of scope). The reference branch that programs the tail is shared bias infrastructure and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: thermal noise density referred to the differential input: both input devices and both PMOS load current sources. A load puts its full noise current into the output, so it is referred to the input by the ratio of its transconductance to the pair's, and it is small only where the load's $g_m$ is kept well below the pair's. The cascodes add little: each is degenerated by the output resistance of the device under it. The tail's noise is common to both sides and cancels at the differential output

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

checks.note: single-stage cascoded gain meets the target
the differential output swing meets the target
